subject: Solaris Dedicated fleet projection & latency SLO mapping
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex@solaristech.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@solaristech.com>

Subject: Estimating committed capacity for Solaris proof-of-production

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profiles looked promising. Procurement asked me to get a concrete Dedicated sizing proposal we can review internally. Two asks: a) an expected tokens/sec profile for the live product (we expect a mix of short chat requests and longer summarization jobs), and b) what Dedicated slab you’d recommend to meet our 200ms P95 SLO for chat while supporting nightly bulk summarization jobs.

I’ve attached a simple usage export (solaris_token_model_v2.xlsx) showing hourly request volumes and a split: 70% short-chat (avg 40 tokens), 30% long-batch (avg 420 tokens), estimated steady-state Q1 traffic: 95 TPS overall, peak bursts to ~350 TPS for 10–15 minute windows.

Can the team map that to tokens/sec, expected latency bands for your recommended model variants, and a proposed safety margin for capacity commitments? Procurement also asked for an estimated committed monthly token burn so they can size the purchase.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a call if useful.

Best,
Alex
Head of AI Product | Solaris Tech
[Attachment: solaris_token_model_v2.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Estimating committed capacity for Solaris proof-of-production

Alex — thanks for the file and the clear traffic split, that’s very helpful. We can give a formal quote but here are the high-level results from a quick simulation run (details and full spreadsheets in the attached).

Summary (high level):
- Input: steady 95 TPS average (70/30 short/long), burst to 350 TPS for ~15 minutes/day.
- Tokens/sec: short-chat path -> ~3,800 tokens/sec; long-batch path -> ~13,300 tokens/sec at peak combined ~17,100 tokens/sec.
- Model variant: recommend Redwood-quant-mistral-12B for chat (low-latency quantized path) and Redwood-quant-mpt-30B for long-batch where throughput dominates. We can run a single mixed-serve pool with heterogeneous instance types and route by model type.
- Latency (baseline, no headroom): chat P95 ≈ 160–190ms, P99 ≈ 320–400ms on a 4-GPU slab of A10G-like instances with continuous batching tuned for short requests. Long-batch completion times depend on token length; throughput-limited jobs will see higher end-to-end times but do not impact chat SLO if routed correctly.

I’ll loop Ben and Karthik to produce a recommended Dedicated slab mix and committed token estimate for procurement.

Sofia
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Solaris - initial throughput model and committed-token sketch

Alex / Sofia — attaching the detailed simulation and token burn projection. Highlights below; see 'solaris_token_model_v2.xlsx' tab 'SimResults' for the hour-by-hour and percentile latencies.

Key assumptions I used (please confirm):
- Short-chat: avg prompt 40 tokens + avg response 120 tokens = 160 tokens per request.
- Long-batch: avg prompt 420 + response 580 = 1,000 tokens per request.
- Q1 expected 95 TPS steady means ~15M tokens/hour steady-state during business hours.
- Burst profile: 15-minute window to 350 TPS (weighted same split) used to size burst headroom.

Estimated token/sec and slab mappings:
- Steady-state token/sec: ~15,200 tokens/sec. Peak burst token/sec: ~27,400 tokens/sec.
- Option A (single slab approach): 4 x 8-GPU slabs with mixed-quant models (2 slabs optimized for low-latency chat; 2 slabs optimized for throughput). This yields P95 chat ≈ 150–180ms, P99 ≈ 330–420ms, with ~1.5x headroom for short bursts.
- Option B (separate pools + aggressive routing): 2 x 8-GPU chat slabs + 3 x 8-GPU batch slabs. Chat pool gives P95 ≈ 120–150ms and a comfortable isolation guarantee; batch pool handles peak summarization with minimal interference. Overall committed footprint is larger but gives better SLO isolation.

Committed token estimate (monthly):
- Using steady-state hour and expected daily peaks, conservative committed month = 1.9B tokens/month. (Spreadsheet line 'CommittedRecommendation').

Attachments: solaris_token_model_v2.xlsx (detailed sim), sla_latency_profile.csv (latency curves).

Next steps: Karthik to propose the GPU SKU mix and rough monthly pricing to feed into procurement.

Ben
Director, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: solaris_token_model_v2.xlsx (xlsx); Attachment: sla_latency_profile.csv (csv)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@solaristech.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 16:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Solaris - initial throughput model and committed-token sketch

Folks — ran the sim across our common GPU SKUs and tuned autotuner profiles. Notes and recommended slab mix below.

Model & Kernel notes:
- Redwood-quant-mistral-12B (4-bit qlinear) provides the best latency/quality trade for chat; it benefits heavily from kernel-level attention fusion on A10G-class hardware.
- Redwood-quant-mpt-30B (8-bit quant) gives much better token/s throughput for long-batch when run in pipeline-parallel on 8-GPU slabs.

Recommended Dedicated footprint (target SLO: chat P95 ≤ 200ms, P99 ≤ 400ms):
- Chat pool: 2 slabs x 8x A10G (or equivalent) tuned for low-concurrency, continuous batching; expected steady capacity handles 120 TPS chat-equivalent (allowing 1.25x buffer over projected chat traffic).
- Batch pool: 2 slabs x 8x A10G (dense packing for high throughput) to absorb nightly summarization and daytime spikes.
- Autoscaling / burst policy: keep 1 additional standby slab (hot spare) in the same region for instantaneous absorption of the 350 TPS 15-min windows; otherwise allow burst to Hosted fallback (costly) if extended beyond 30 minutes.

Headroom and safety multiplier: recommend committing to 1.6x the steady-state tokens/sec to give margins for demand variance, model upgrades, and unmodeled client behavior. For Solaris that yields the 1.9B tokens/month Ben quoted as a conservative purchase. If Solaris prefers a tighter budget, we can reduce to 1.3x but we’d ask for a short-term overage buffer (billing overages or short-term burst credits).

Failure modes & graceful degradation mapping:
- If chat pool saturates: route lower-priority diagnostic routes to quantized fallback models (smaller MTL variants) and maintain chat SLOs for critical traffic.
- If batch pool backlogs: defer non-urgent summarization to overnight windows or use rate-limited batch queuing with user notification.

Deliverables I’ll provide by EOD Thursday: detailed SKU-level quote, expected token burn by slab, and suggested rollout phasing (pilot -> ramp -> commit).

Karthik
Sr. Infra Eng, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Alex — thanks for the detailed ask and team for the quick turnaround. A couple of business / procurement items to close the loop:

2) Pilot phasing recommendation
- Phase 1 (30 days): 1 chat slab + 1 batch slab, focused on validating routing and SLOs during peak windows. Measure token burn vs sim and tune batching profiles.
- Phase 2 (next 60 days): add the second slab for each pool and move to committed billing.

3) Next steps for Solaris procurement
- If Procurement is comfortable with Core, we’ll share the DocuSign and a SKU-level invoice. If you’d like Lean, we’ll mark the overage guardrails and define temporary burst credits.

Alex — can you confirm whether Solaris prefers Core or Lean, and whether legal needs any additional SLA wording? I’ll attach the quote and a one-page runbook for the pilot to the HubSpot deal after you confirm.

Best,
Marissa Cole
